answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can submit bids, with rewards and voting weight capped by that deposit. If identities are linked to the same operator, suspicious clusters can be challenged and lose their stake when evidence confirms duplication. This does not make Sybils impossible, but raises their marginal cost: an attacker must tie up real capital for each identity and risk losing it, often longer than the horizon for a quick exploit. A zephyr of cheap accounts cannot harvest an orchard of rewards without paying that cost.
